result.summary: This PR adds cmake install rules so that bash and fish completion scripts under contrib/completions/ are installed alongside their corresponding binaries, including for component-based installs. It extends the existing install_binary_component helper (following the HAS_MANPAGE pattern) with HAS_BASH_COMPLETION and HAS_FISH_COMPLETION keywords, and adds INSTALL_BASH_COMPLETIONS/INSTALL_FISH_COMPLETIONS options (both default ON).
result.problem: Packagers currently have to manually copy shell completion scripts from contrib/completions/ into system directories when packaging Bitcoin Core; this PR automates that via cmake install so packages ship working tab-completion out of the box.

open_concerns: purpleKarrot's broader architectural critique that install_binary_component is becoming an unwieldy convenience wrapper and that fine-grained install components would be better; hebasto disagreed, citing precedent in LLVM/Qt, no consensus reached but not treated as blocking.

fanquake questioned whether the project will actually maintain these scripts long-term, given lack of historical contributor interest in related PRs (#33385, #33402, #33747); author responded that the alternative is not shipping them at all, and prefers to maintain them.
resolved_concerns: ryanofsky, BrandonOdiwuor, and 151henry151 all flagged inconsistency between the if(EXISTS) approach and the explicit HAS_MANPAGE-style keyword pattern used for manpages; author addressed this by force-pushing a version using explicit HAS_BASH_COMPLETION/HAS_FISH_COMPLETION keywords and split install options.
luke-jr suggested separate options per shell since users are unlikely to use multiple shells; implemented as INSTALL_BASH_COMPLETIONS and INSTALL_FISH_COMPLETIONS.

categories.rationale: This automates a manual packaging step ('Packagers currently need to copy shell completion scripts... into the appropriate system directories') which is a real but narrow convenience for distro packagers and end users who want working tab-completion out of the box. It does not touch release integrity, reproducibility, or supported-platform builds, and fanquake raised an open question about whether the project even wants to commit to maintaining these scripts long-term.

uncertainties: Whether the project will commit to maintaining the bash/fish completion scripts long-term is still an open, unresolved question raised by fanquake, though it does not block this PR's mechanics.
purpleKarrot's deeper architectural objection to the install_binary_component pattern was not fully resolved; unclear if it will resurface to block merge.
result.card: This PR adds cmake install rules to automatically install bash and fish shell completion scripts alongside their binaries, extending the existing HAS_MANPAGE-style install_binary_component pattern with HAS_BASH_COMPLETION/HAS_FISH_COMPLETION keywords and per-shell install options. It solves a real but narrow packaging annoyance: packagers currently copy completion scripts manually, and multiple reviewers (BrandonOdiwuor, 151henry151, caesrcd) tested that installs now work correctly, including with --component and DESTDIR staging. The author just force-pushed to address ryanofsky's and others' concern about using if(EXISTS) versus explicit keywords, following the manpage pattern, so the PR is now Ready for review. One deeper design objection from purpleKarrot about the install_binary_component wrapper's growing scope remains open but was met with a counter-rationale from hebasto and not pressed further. fanquake raised an unresolved question about whether the project wants to commit to maintaining these scripts at all, given past unmerged completion PRs. No dependencies; fixes issue #34714.
